title: Black Gradient Windowskin for Title Command Menu

posts.author: Tw0Face
posts.body:
Hi guys, is it possible to have the Windowskin of only the Title Command Menu appear in borderless semi-transparent black (or dark grey) with a well defined gradient (black-to-fully-transparent) at the bottom and top just like seen in the Spoiler tag below? I want to be able to do this to my VX ACE games. It's purely cosmetic, but I'm looking for a style like that as it can highly improve RPG Maker Titlescreens and make it look more modern and up-to-date instead of using the default RM box graphic.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
yes, this is possible.
the best way is probably a dedicated script for this, and there I can't help.
however if you can't get such a script then a secondary option is to work with a windowskin changer.
you would have to use a fake border for the gradient effect, and then change the windowskin to the regular one as soon as you leave the title screen.
Windowskin Changer
By default, RPG Maker uses the file called "Window" stored in the Graphics/System folder, and only supports one windowskin throughout the game.This script allows you to change window skins dyn

posts.author: kyonides
posts.body:
Version 2:
Ruby:
# * Window_Title's Gradient Backdrop ACE * #
#   Scripter : Kyonides Arkanthes
#   2024-10-02

class Scene_Title
  alias :kyon_title_grad_scn_ttl_crt_cmd_win :create_command_window
  def create_command_window
    kyon_title_grad_scn_ttl_crt_cmd_win
    command_window_gradient_effect
  end

  def command_window_gradient_effect
    @command_window.opacity = 0
    cww = @command_window.width
    cwh = @command_window.height
    lines = @command_window.item_max * 24
    @command_sprite = Sprite.new
    @command_sprite.x = @command_window.x
    @command_sprite.y = @command_window.y
    @command_sprite.bitmap = bit = Bitmap.new(cww, cwh)
    rect = Rect.new(0, 12, bit.width, lines)
    border = Rect.new(0, 0, bit.width, 12)
    color1 = Color.new(0, 0, 0, 24)
    color2 = Color.new(0, 0, 0, 192)
    bit.gradient_fill_rect(border, color1, color2, true)
    bit.fill_rect(rect, color2)
    border.y += lines + 12
    bit.gradient_fill_rect(border, color2, color1, true)
  end

  def close_command_window
    @command_window.cursor_rect.empty
    rect = @command_sprite.src_rect
    hmax = rect.height / 2
    until rect.y == hmax
      rect.y += 4
      rect.height -= 8
      @command_sprite.y += 4
      @command_window.contents_opacity -= 26
      update
    end
    @command_sprite.bitmap.dispose
    @command_sprite.dispose
  end
end
